page.h1: HTS Chapter 26: Ores, Slag and Ash — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariff on U.S. Copper Concentrate & Iron Ore by Country (HTS Ch. 26) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Mexico, Canada, the EU, Korea, Japan, China, the UK and Taiwan charge on U.S. copper, zinc, lead and moly concentrate, iron ore and slag.

intro: Seven of the eight largest markets let U.S. ores, concentrates, slag and ash in **duty-free**. Mexico and Canada charge 0% under USMCA (and 0% as their normal rate), Korea under KORUS, and the EU, Japan, the UK and Taiwan charge 0% on every Chapter 26 line from any supplier. **China** is the exception: its normal rate is 0% on ores and 4% on slag and ash, but U.S. goods add the 10% extra duty and, unless the importer holds an exclusion, a 2018–2019 counter-tariff of 10–25%. That makes **35%** on copper and zinc concentrate and iron ore pellets, 20% on lead and molybdenum concentrate and 10% on iron ore fines. With tariffs this low, access depends on the buyer's rules: waste-import controls for slag and residues, China's ban on solid-waste imports and the EU carbon border mechanism for iron ore pellets (see each market's regulator).
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Mexico ($2.42B, up 31.9%) is almost all copper concentrate (2603, $2.28B) for its smelters, plus molybdenum concentrate ($88M). Mexico's normal rate on ores is already 0%, so U.S. ore enters free with or without a USMCA certificate, and its January 2026 tariff increases skipped Chapter 26.
profile.mainProducts: Copper ore & concentrates (2603) · Molybdenum ore & concentrates (2613)

regulator.name: SEMARNAT (hazardous waste imports) and SAT importer registry
regulator.requirement: Ores and concentrates need no product approval; the importer must be in the importers' registry (Padrón de Importadores). Slag, ash and residues that Mexico classes as hazardous waste need a SEMARNAT import authorization

profile.headline: Canada ($2.40B, up 4.6%) buys copper concentrate ($774M), zinc concentrate ($535M), iron ore, mostly pellets ($411M), lead concentrate ($316M), nickel concentrate ($148M) and metal-bearing residues ($139M) for its smelters and steel mills. All of it enters free, and none of Canada's counter-tariff orders of 2025 or 2026 lists a Chapter 26 good.
profile.mainProducts: Copper ore & concentrates (2603) · Zinc ore & concentrates (2608)

regulator.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (hazardous waste and hazardous recyclable material permits)
regulator.requirement: Ores and concentrates need no import permit. Slag, ash or residues that count as hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material need a permit under the Cross-border Movement of Hazardous Waste and Hazardous Recyclable Material Regulations before they enter

profile.headline: The EU ($1.52B, up 22.7%) buys molybdenum concentrate, mostly through the Netherlands ($665M in all), zinc concentrate for smelters in Spain and Belgium ($402M), and gold and copper ores for Germany. Every Chapter 26 line is free from any supplier, so the EU–U.S. framework of July 2026 changed nothing here.
profile.mainProducts: Molybdenum ore & concentrates (2613) · Zinc ore & concentrates (2608)
profile.tariffNow: Free (0% EU tariff on all suppliers)

regulator.name: European Commission (CBAM for iron ore pellets; Waste Shipment Regulation for residues)
regulator.requirement: Ores and concentrates need no approval. Agglomerated iron ore (2601.12) is a CBAM good: since January 1, 2026 the EU importer must be an authorised CBAM declarant and report the emissions embedded in the pellets. Slag, ash and residues shipped as waste follow Regulation (EU) 2024/1157

assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in November 2026. They come from the WITS (TRAINS) MFN applied rate for one six-digit subheading per heading, the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 2603.00 for copper concentrate, 2601.12 for iron ore pellets, 2613.10 for roasted molybdenum concentrate and 2616.90 for gold ores), for 2023, the latest year WITS holds. EU rates were checked in TARIC for iron ore pellets, zinc concentrate and roasted molybdenum. National 8–10-digit lines can differ.

Every market shown except Korea and China has a 0% MFN rate on every Chapter 26 line. Mexico, Canada and Korea show the free-trade-agreement rate; Korea's normal-rate column shows the 2% that slag and ash pay without KORUS origin.

China's cells add three layers: China's MFN rate (0% on ores, 4% on slag and ash; no Chapter 26 line has a 2026 provisional rate), the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods, and the 2018–2019 counter-tariff of the line (25%, 20% or 10%, or none). An importer with an exclusion pays only the first two. A range shows that lines in the heading differ.
Trade agreements that are signed or announced but not in force (Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, India) are not applied; see Tariff updates.
